items.stem: A support answer must name the source of each claim. The response must stay free text, with no JSON schema. Which change meets both constraints?
options: Ask the model in the prompt to list sources after each claim.
Pass each chunk as a search result block with source and title, and enable citations.
Pass each chunk as search results with citations disabled, and add a reranker before the call.
Enable structured outputs with a source field for each claim.
items.rationale: Each citation links a claim to a search result block that carries your source and title. Citations are disabled by default, so the request must enable them.
items.trap: A prompt that asks for sources looks equivalent, but the names are not tied to retrieved blocks, so you cannot check them (Inference).

items.stem: A policy document has tables split across chunks, and answers cite the wrong row. Each citation must point to one table row.
options: Keep sentence chunking, and switch to a larger generation model.
Send each table as a plain text document, and switch to the largest embedding model.
Build one custom content block per table row, sent as a custom content document.
Turn on contextual retrieval, so the table rows group automatically.
items.rationale: Custom content documents keep your blocks as they are, with no further chunking. Each row block can then be cited on its own.
items.trap: Contextual retrieval looks like a table fix, but the docs do not describe it.

items.stem: The right passage appears in the candidate list, but it ranks low. The answer model needs that passage among the top passages. Which two changes meet the ranking constraint?
options: Switch to a larger generation model, with the same candidate list.
Add a reranker that reorders the candidate list for the query.
Set input_type to None on the query embedding, so ranking uses raw similarity.
Send only the top reranked passages to the answer model.
items.rationale: A reranker returns candidates in relevance order for the query. The top reranked passages then reach the answer model.
items.trap: A larger generation model looks like the fix, but it does not change the candidate order (Inference).
